INSTRUMENT READ AT SOURCE: Land Development Code Chapter 25-2, Subchapter C, Article 2, Division 1, Section 25-2-492 (Site Development Regulations), Subsection (D) site development regulation table — read live 2026-09-16 from a browser render of the Municode page at https://library.municode.com/tx/austin/codes/land_development_code?nodeId=TIT25LADE_CH25-2ZO_SUBCHAPTER_CUSDERE_ART2PRUSDERE_DIV1RETA_S25-2-492SIDERE , whose code is 'Codified through Ordinance No. 20260122-059, effective February 2, 2026 (Supp. No. 173)' and whose table-level Source line ends 'Ord. No. 20251023-063, Pt. 1, 11-3-25' (CBD 350 ft maximum height, effective 2025-11-03). NOTE ON CHANNEL - HOW THIS TEXT WAS OBTAINED (expanded 2026-09-16 per the wave planner's F-1): the same section's Source line shows the table was amended by Ord. No. 20231207-001, Pt. 5, 12-18-23 (HOME phase 2). ROUTE, STATED PLAINLY: the Subsection (D) text above was obtained by BROWSER RENDER - the citation_url was opened in an in-IDE Chromium browser on 2026-09-16 and Subsection (D) was read out of the rendered DOM (the district columns, the footnote superscript markers and the 'Codified through ...' stamp), then transcribed column-aware. verified by the author through browser render of this URL; a plain fetch of this URL returns only the Municode application shell (planner, 2026-09-16T21:05Z). The author reproduced that same limitation: a plain HTTP GET of the citation_url, and of the legacy .../HTML/15302/level5/... form of it, each returns a ~6 KB Angular shell (ng-app='mcc.library_desktop', serverProps carrying libraryApiUrl '/api' plus azureCodesBlobUrlPrefix, and an 'Internet Explorer not supported' block) with no ordinance text at all. Other routes tried, so a successor lane does not repeat them: www.municode.com/webcontent/austintx/25-2-492.xlsx (the Excel download the elaws mirror advertises) -> HTTP 404; library.municode.com/api/library/tx/austin -> HTTP 401; the blob-prefix root mcclibrary.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/codecontent/ -> HTTP 404, because content blobs are addressed by per-document GUIDs that are not enumerable. The City's own LDC page (austintexas.gov/planning/city-and-land-development-code) links only to Municode, so there is no City-hosted PDF of the codified table to fall back on. As of 2026-09-16 NO plain-fetch URL returns the CURRENT table, so this row set's citation_url stays the browser-renderable Municode page. PLAIN-FETCH CORROBORATOR, NOT A CITATION: http://austin-tx.elaws.us/code/ldc_title25_ch25-2_subchc_art2_div1_sec25-2-492 does return the table text to a plain fetch, and aligned column-for-column it agrees with the browser render on all 37 districts for FRONT YARD and on 36 of 37 for MAXIMUM HEIGHT; but it carries no 'codified through' stamp and is pre-2025-11-03 exactly where it matters - its CBD MAXIMUM HEIGHT cell is blank and the string '350' appears nowhere in it (it is also stale on MAXIMUM DWELLING UNITS PER LOT: SF-1/SF-2/SF-3 1/1/[blank] vs 3/3/3). It corroborates the values read; it cannot serve as the citation, because it does not carry the current table. MODELING NOTES: (1) em-dash cells — many yard and coverage cells print an em dash where Subsection (D) states no numeric standard; those are served as sentinels (0 ft for yards, 100 for coverage/impervious percent, 999 for height) with not_specified: true, which the acceptance gate treats as an honest gap rather than a value. (2) footnote-marker cells — where a cell carries a footnote number instead of a number, the row was read from the section the footnote names (fn 4 -> 25-2-779 SF-4A; fn 5 -> 25-2-558 SF-4B; fn 11 -> 25-2-584 W/LO; fn 12 -> 25-2-582 CH; fn 13 -> 25-2-601 IP/MI/LI; fn 14 -> 25-2-603 R&D; fn 15 -> 25-2-623 AV; fn 17 -> 25-2-625 P). (3) adjacency- and gradient-graded cells (IP/MI/LI and R&D yards, CH height, LA impervious) are carried as low-confidence required-by-schema placeholders with not_specified: true, never as a silent pick — the tier text is quoted in each provenance entry. (4) NO ROW, by design: TOD, NBG, ERC and TND are not in the Euclidean Subsection (D) table at all — they are Subchapter E (Design Standards and Mixed Use) districts whose rules are form-based building-placement standards (Subchapter E Arts. 1-4, esp. Art. 2 Site Development Standards), which this Euclidean 7-scalar shape cannot carry; UNZ is unzoned land with no district standards; and the MH column of Subsection (D) is em dashes throughout with no MH district-regulations section anywhere in Chapter 25-2 Subchapter C Article 3. (5) KNOWN CONFLICT NOT TOUCHED: the pre-existing MF-2 and MF-3 rows in this file carry front_ft 15; the current Municode table states 25 ft for both MF-2 (=fn 7 -> 25-2-561) and MF-3 (=fn 8 -> 25-2-562), and a second live source (the §25-2-563 comparison table reproduced in City of Austin edims documents 249719/250098) shows MF-2/MF-3 FRONT YARD 25/25 against MF-4/MF-5/MF-6 15/15/15. Those rows were not researched by this lane and are left exactly as found; the disagreement is reported upward rather than silently corrected or silently matched. P-299 OT-1 (height-flag reconciliation, 2026-09-17): every max_height_ft row in this file that carried not_specified was re-read against its own provenance quote and classified with this repo's not_specified-meaning instrument (doc_repo scripts/corpus_not_specified_audit.py, OPS-21-R1). FLAG REMOVED, VALUE KEPT -- here the FLAG was the defect and the number was real; not_specified on these rows asserted a false absence. The basis is stated PER ROW because it is not the same for all of them: for these rows the quote names the tabulated height column without restating the number, so the basis is the OPS-21-R1 / P-146 instrument's classification REAL_VALUE_FLAGGED -- the values across that row's flagged siblings are VARIED (transcribed numbers, not one uniform placeholder), which is the discriminator the ruling names (SF-1 Single-Family Residence Large Lot (keeps 35); SF-2 Single-Family Residence Standard Lot (keeps 35); SF-3 Family Residence (keeps 35); MF-1 Multifamily Residence Limited Density (keeps 40); MF-2 Multifamily Residence Low Density (keeps 40); MF-3 Multifamily Residence Medium Density (keeps 40); MF-4 Multifamily Residence Moderate-High Density (keeps 60); MF-5 Multifamily Residence High Density (keeps 60); MF-6 Multifamily Residence Highest Density (keeps 90)). Reason, from this file's own note above: every value here was read through a COPY of the governing instrument rather than off the instrument's own text -- browser render of the Municode page (read out of the rendered DOM; a plain fetch returns only the Angular application shell; an eLaws mirror was used only as a corroborator, not as the citation). The state is not a downgrade of the read's quality; it is the honest name for the channel, and it keeps "primary-source-verified" meaning what it says for the tables that did reach the instrument's own text. It is treated exactly like primary-source-verified for rule G2 (no code-section atom is required) and skips G5's quote round-trip for the same reason.
